stops.note: 'to assess, value', perhaps from tangere 'to touch'; the same verb gives English 'tax'
from Medieval Latin taxa 'charge' + Greek metron 'measure'; Wilhelm Bruhn built the fare meter in 1891, and the first motor taxi, a Daimler Victoria with a meter, ran in Stuttgart in 1897
taximeter + cabriolet; Harry N. Allen launched a fleet of meter-fitted French-built cabs in New York in 1907
clipped from taxicab; London's black cabs had to pass 'the Knowledge' of city streets, a test set up in 1865

current_meaning: a car with a driver that carries passengers for a fare
